headline: High-risk overlap: nullclaw can read/write and use MCP/network, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list with no direct ingestion path, so most pairwise risks are limited but B/C/D remain plausible via workspace or MCP…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest nullclaw output. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or an external workspace/MCP path on nullclaw, which is not documented as shared here. That makes injection possible only under unusual operator setup and with small blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies nullclaw output into awesome-selfhosted content or metadata
IF nullclaw is connected to a shared MCP or workspace channel that feeds awesome-selfhosted
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the pair
Keep awesome-selfhosted read-only during review
Paste only sanitized excerpts into any curation workflow
Use a separate scratch file for nullclaw outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent transfer

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes, but nullclaw reads and writes workspace files, audit logs, and secrets, and can egress broadly. If both are pointed at the same workspace or files, nullclaw can expose sensitive material through its outputs or network calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default nullclaw deployments, though not proven for this specific pair.
conditions: IF nullclaw is configured to access a workspace containing secrets or private documents
IF awesome-selfhosted content is stored in the same filesystem tree that nullclaw reads or writes
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different directories
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Disable broad egress for nullclaw during curation
Review nullclaw audit logs for sensitive filenames
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or execution surface, so it cannot contend for mutable state itself. nullclaw, however, can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; if the operator places both agents over the same repo or workspace, nullclaw can race with human edits or external automation. The conflict is therefore real but depends on shared mutable resources.
conditions: IF nullclaw and another editor share the same git checkout or workspace
IF nullclaw is allowed to modify files while the curation process is active
mitigations: Use a read-only checkout for awesome-selfhosted review
Pause nullclaw writes before editing shared files
Commit changes from only one actor at a time
Keep separate git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by nullclaw when building workflows or recommendations. nullclaw can act on inputs via shell, browser, git, and MCP, so a mistaken listing or malformed metadata could cascade into downstream actions if the operator wires the pair together without verification. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes awesome-selfhosted entries as authoritative configuration or task input
IF downstream automation is enabled for nullclaw based on curated list content
mitigations: Require human review before acting on list-derived items
Validate entries against the source repo before use
Limit nullclaw to read-only browsing for this workflow
Log provenance for every imported item
requires-engineering: add schema validation for imported records

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is evidenced in either profile. awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source list, while nullclaw handles secrets and logs, so the main compliance concern is accidental placement of regulated data into nullclaw-managed workspaces. Because the pair itself does not establish a specific jurisdictional or certification conflict, this remains a low, conditional risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in nullclaw workspace files or logs
IF the operator uses the pair for data subject or residency-sensitive records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of nullclaw workspaces
Disable unnecessary logging for sensitive sessions
Review retention settings before importing records
Use a separate environment for compliance-sensitive work
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
